title: Cultural Humility in Caring for People with Serious Illness
usable_for: anchors cultural humility as a power-aware stance; not a substitute for tradition-holder authority
do_not_use_for: ritual instruction, sacred practice disclosure, or tradition authority
universal claims about all members of a tradition, ethnicity, religion, caste, lineage, congregation, family, or diaspora
legal, funeral, clinical, disposition, cemetery, crematory, hospital-policy, or body-transport advice
replacing clergy, chaplains, imams, rabbis, priests, ministers, elders, celebrants, funeral directors, local law, or the family’s stated wishes
publishing private, identifiable, child, restricted, ceremonial, or community-governed material without explicit review and consent
extraction_rules: extract vocabulary, scene context, source bias, and review gates, not how-to steps
preserve exact tradition/community terms and variant spellings where supplied
mark commercial or secondary summaries as low-weight and never authoritative
route all practice questions to local tradition holders and local law
treat refusal, silence, and non-disclosure as legitimate data boundaries
